day_shape: 68 items: Strait of Hormuz tanker incident with IRGC turn-back order and UKMTO fire report, Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact activated after Yemeni missile strikes on Riyadh, Israel marks October 7 third anniversary, two more Isfahan protesters executed; nothing from UK Parliament.

threads.label: Hormuz tanker incident and sanctions warnings
threads.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker ordered by Iran's IRGC to turn back in the Strait of Hormuz or risk being hit, with Defa Press citing a later fire report on an oil tanker there. The Jerusalem Post reported the US warned foreign banks of sanctions over Iran dealings, and Khamenei's office claimed enemy forces have been expelled from the Arabian Sea.

threads.label: Yemen offensive and Riyadh strikes
threads.summary: Yemeni government forces launched a three-front offensive against Houthi territory with Saudi air support, while Iran International reported Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated their Mecca Joint Defense Agreement in Riyadh. IRIB claimed Yemeni missiles struck Riyadh's Al-Misfah neighbourhood and halted airport operations; Houthi officials denied Saudi media accounts of Mokha falling.

threads.label: October 7 third anniversary in Israel
threads.summary: Israel marked three years since the Hamas attack with nationwide memorials, documentary broadcasts, and former hostage testimonies, while the Times of Israel reported new PTSD diagnoses doubled in the year after the attack. The Jerusalem Post cited an Israeli source saying 4,000 of the 6,000 infiltrators have been killed, and London's Metropolitan Police urged organisers to move an October 7 pro-Palestinian march.

threads.label: IDF Gaza and Syria operations
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Ibrahim Mustafa Suleiman Abu Awaimer, a Hamas Nukhba platoon commander who entered Israel on October 7, in a strike on Nuseirat. IDF troops also reported apprehending two suspects on a motorcycle near a post in southern Syria and firing on a vehicle after an attempted ramming near Bani Naim.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure and executions
threads.summary: Iran International and the Jerusalem Post reported Iran executed two more men detained over January 2026 Isfahan protests, bringing the Alikhani Square case total to seven. Iran International also reported stepped-up Starlink warnings and worker complaints of delayed wages and lost benefits, while Pezeshkian nominated Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as defense minister.

threads.label: flydubai hijacking fallout and UK bomber withdrawal
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported passengers on flydubai flight 1073 feared diversion to Iran or Yemen after a thwarted hijacking, and US Vice President JD Vance said he had seen nothing conclusive on an Iranian role. The US also removed its bomber fleet from a British airbase a week after five arrests nearby over a suspected Iranian plot.

threads.label: Netanyahu-Tehran rhetorical exchange and missile programme
threads.summary: Iran International reported Netanyahu predicted the fall of Iran's leadership while Iran's armed forces chief warned any new conflict would engulf the region. The Jerusalem Post cited an IRGC spokesperson saying Iran's military will work to develop longer-range missiles.

events.summary_en: Saudi efforts for 'media victory' in Yemen. Hizam al-Asad, member of the political office of the Houthis movement in Yemen, denied Saudi media claims about the advance of Saudi-backed mercenaries in Bab al-Mandab and Mokha. Al-Asad, in a message posted on his personal page, said that only Yemeni armed forces and residents of Bab al-Mandab, Dhubab and Mokha are present in these areas. He also said that Saudi mercenaries who were intending this morning to advance from the province of Lahj faced the storm of Yemeni armed forces. Al-Asad, referring to the fact that Saudi Arabia is seeking to score a 'media victory', said that once again their false claims about fictitious victories have been exposed.

events.title: A Hamas terrorist who participated in the October 7 onslaught was killed in an Israeli strike over the weekend, the IDF and Shin Bet announce. The strike on Friday in central Gaza's Nuseirat killed Ibrahim Mustafa Suleiman Abu Awaimer, identified by the IDF as a platoon commander in Hamas's elite Nukhba Force, who invaded Israel on October 7, 2023. The IDF says that recently, Abu Awaimer was involved in advancing attacks on troops and Israeli civilians, as well as restoring Hamas capabilities, "in systematic violation of the ceasefire," adding that he was killed to "remove the threat he posed."

events.title: Proposal of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Regarding Transactions Involving the A7 Network's Sub-Agents
events.summary: FinCEN is issuing a finding and notice of proposed rulemaking, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Public Law 116-283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81), finding transactions involving any company operating outside of the United States that is controlled by the A7 Network, a sanctions evasion and money laundering service with ties to Russia, leveraged by a wide range of illicit actors, including Iran and its terrorist proxies, to be a class of transactions of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance and proposing the imposition of a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds, by any covered financial institution, involving that class of transactions.
